description: An interactive STEM-based space simulation where students become junior astronauts, explore planets, manage life-support resources, solve mission challenges, and survive space emergencies. The experience builds scientific curiosity, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills while inspiring the next generation of space explorers.
summary: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is a classroom-friendly space mission survival simulator designed to help students understand the challenges astronauts face during space exploration. Through a hands-on physical mission station and decision-based simulation, learners take the role of a mission crew and manage essential resources such as oxygen, water, food and electrical power. They respond to simulated challenges including power shortages, water conservation, communication delays and equipment alerts. The project integrates habitat and life-support systems, solar power, a Bio-Orbit greenhouse, rover exploration and mission control. It encourages scientific thinking, resource management, teamwork, mathematical reasoning and evidence-based decision-making. By combining a physical model with interactive mission scenarios, the project makes space exploration more accessible and engaging for young learners.
details:
The Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an educational space mission survival simulator designed to introduce students to the practical challenges of human space exploration.

The project consists of a physical mission station representing a space habitat, with labelled resource meters, a solar-power indicator, a greenhouse, a rover and a mission control desk. Learners participate in decision-based simulations using scenario cards or a simple digital dashboard.

The simulation follows five stages: Brief, Check, Decide, Monitor and Debrief. During each mission, learners monitor oxygen, water, food and electrical power while responding to unexpected events such as power shortages, water conservation challenges, communication delays and equipment alerts.

The system includes six core modules: Resource Control, Habitat and Life Support, Solar Power, Bio-Orbit Greenhouse, Rover and Exploration, and Mission Control.

The working model can be constructed using cardboard or foam board, transparent plastic sheets, coloured paper, straws, craft sticks, printed resource gauges, movable sliders, optional LEDs and a battery pack. Scenario cards and a paper mission log are used to record decisions and mission outcomes.

NASA open data can strengthen the simulation by providing real-world information about solar conditions, Mars rover exploration and Earth observation. Specific datasets will be selected, checked and applied to inform mission decisions.

The project integrates science, mathematics, engineering and teamwork. It helps learners understand resource management, systems thinking, mission planning and evidence-based decision-making.

This is an educational simulation for classroom learning, not a real astronaut training system.
